cues.text: Thank you for joining me for this brief
tutorial focused on managing pipette
devices within the ArtelWare
application. I have a lot of great
information to share with you. So, let's
go ahead and get started. Prior to
creating my pipette entry, I have already
created the pipette's owner and location.
Now, let's explore how we add a pipette.
There are a few different ways on how to
add a pipette into the ArtelWare software
application. But before I get started,
let me just make a note that we've made
the work easy for you. We have preloaded
a pipette catalog that has a majority of
the pipette brands, manufacturers, and
models already preloaded into it. Now,
if you don't see the pipette that you're
working with in our catalog, there's a
really easy way to add that, but I'll go
ahead and cover that in a little bit.
Now, as I mentioned, there's a couple of
different ways to add a pipette into the
ArtelWare application. The first is to
click on the add device shortcut that's
on the get started bar. Another way is
to navigate to the configuration screen
of the software and click on the pipette
section. But for today, I'm going to go
ahead and select the add device shortcut
on the get started bar. Once I select
add device, I'll make sure that pipette is
highlighted and then I'll click okay.
Now in this new pipette screen, it's
important to note that any field that
has the red asterisk is a required
field. So the first field that we have
to complete is the selection of the
manufacturer and the model. Let's go
ahead and click on the ellipsus to see
what we have. Now the way that you
select your pipette manufacturer is by
clicking on the dropdown that you see at
the top left side corner of the screen.
You can navigate through this dropdown
and you can see that there's a lot of
pipette manufacturers again that are
already listed for you. We're going to
select Apendorf today because I'm
working with an Appondorf reference
pipette. Now once you select the
manufacturer, all the models that are
shown are distinct to that manufacturer
that you've selected. Sometimes it can
be hard to navigate through that list.
So what I like to do is I like to click
on the max volume column header so that
it sorts everything in order for me. So
today I'm using a 2 to 20 microL
research ependorf pipette. So I'll go
ahead and select research. It's a
variable pipette as I mentioned 2 to 20
microL. The catalog ID that you see
there, that's the catalog ID for
Appendorf. We'll go ahead and select
okay. And then once you select okay,
these next three fields will
automatically populate. The ISO device
type, the number of channels, and the
volume range. Let's go ahead and scroll
down and see what other fields we have
to complete. The pipette ID field is the
next field that we need to complete. So
there are a couple of things that you
have to note about the pipette ID field.
Number one, special characters and
spaces are not accepted, but it's okay
if you forget because the software will
remind you.
The second thing about the pipette ID
field is that once you've entered it and
you click save at the bottom of the
screen, you cannot edit nor change the
pipette ID. So you'll want to make sure
that you're very deliberate about the
pipette ID that you've entered in. Now,
your pipette ID can be the serial number
that's etched on the pipette itself, or it
can be an internal asset ID. The pipette
ID that I'm using today is an internal
asset ID number. And I'm going to go
ahead and add an underscoreb to its ID.
The description field is an optional
field, so we'll go ahead and leave that
alone. Now, the serial number field is
also optional, but the serial number is
different than the pipeet ID itself. The
serial number is a unique identifier
that's etched on the pipette itself. So,
let me go ahead and populate that
information in. Next, we have to select
the location for this pipette. Now, what
our tailware will do is automatically
assign the location that's listed first
alphabetically in your location list,
but I'm going to go ahead and select a
different location. And then I'm also
going to select an owner for this pipette.
Now again before I click save really
really important thing to note is I want
to confirm that that pipette ID is exactly
what I'd like for it to be. And in this
particular case I'm just going to make
one quick change and I'll verify
everything that I' I've entered in yet
one more time and then I'll click save.
Now our TWware has the ability to
generate barcode ID labels and they're
really wonderful. They help make the
calibration process really efficient
especially if you've got a lot of pipe
at your facility. Usually what I do is
once I've created a pipette, I'll go ahead
and create a barcode ID label by
clicking on the printer icon and
selecting pipette label.
And now I've got a beautiful barcode ID
label that I can attach to my pipette. Now
remember earlier I talked about what
happens if you have a pipette model that's
not in the catalog. So let's say that
you go and you look at the the
manufacturer list. The pipette that I'm
working with today is a Niro pipette, a
nichi pet. But I don't see Niro listed
as a manufacturer in this catalog.
So from here I can easily add a new
pipette model by clicking on the plus sign
to add a new pipette model to the catalog.
And from here I can go ahead and add the
pipette manufacturer and the model of the
pipette. The pipette catalog ID. Now that's
a field that is required and that's
Niro's pipette catalog ID. If you don't
happen to have that ID, it's okay. You
can just populate that with any type of
field that you'd like. It's not
important for how our Telware will
calibrate your pipettes. The ISO device
type is important. Most pipettes are ISO
device type A. They're air displacement
pipettes. The number of channels is
important as well as whether or not this
is a fixed or variable pipette. In this
particular case, this is a variable
volume pipette. And with a variable
volume pipette, you have to enter in the
lowest volume and the highest volume
that it can run. So this is a 10 to 100
microL variable pipette.
Now, we're not quite finished. So you
might be really tempted to click that
add pipette to catalog button. However,
you need to enter some manufacturer
specifications.
So, before I click on this enter
manufacturer specifications, you might
be wondering where do I get those from?
Well, usually you get those from the
pipette manufacturer website. Oftentimes,
pipette manufacturers will list their
pipette specifications on their websites
or in their operator manuals. When you
have a variable volume pipette, you have
to enter the manufacturer specifications
for the lowest range and the highest
range at minimum. If you have the
mid-range manufacturer specification,
you can certainly enter that as well.
So, let's go ahead and click on enter
manufacturer specifications. The lowest
range volume for this pipette is 10. The
pipette manufacturer list in accuracy spec
as 7 and then precision spec is 045. So,
I'll go ahead and select add for that.
Now remember this is a variable volume
pipette. So I need to add the lowest
volume manufacturer spec as well as the
highest volume manufacturer spec. So
I'll go ahead and enter 100 and enter
the manufacturer spec for that as well.
And then once I've entered in all of my
manufacturer specifications, I'll go
ahead and select okay. And I'll select
add pipette to catalog. And by default,
you'll see that now our Telware shows
the manufacturer that I just added. And
if I click on the manufacturer dropdown,
you'll see that Nuriro is now added
there as well. Now, when you're adding
pipettes to our Telword, we've built in a
couple of things to help make your job a
bit easier. Let's say that you have a
lot of pipettes that are all the same type
of pipettes. So, for example, if I go to
the configuration screen and I go to my
pipettes list, perhaps I've got nine more
pipettes that are just like this appendorf
research pipette that I entered in
earlier. You have this wonderful clone
icon. And what it will do is it will
bring over all of the pipette information
for you. And all that you'll need to do
is make sure that the pipette ID is
properly assigned and anything else
that's on this bottom half of the screen
is properly assigned. Now you can change
things on the top half as well, but
again that clone icon really saves you a
lot of time. Also within the same screen
you have the option to export your pipette
lists. So if you wanted a list of your
pipettes, which would also include when
they're last calibrated and when their
next calibration date is due, you can
certainly do that. You can also choose
to print a full-size printout um or a
PDF of your pipe head inventory from the
screen as well. You've got a couple of
different icons that are here. You have
a filter icon, a refresh icon. You've
also got an add icon, and you've got an
edit icon as well. So, let's go ahead
and talk about these other icons over on
the right hand side because you'll
notice there's a deactivate pipette icon
there. If you have a pipe pet that's
that you need to deactivate because
you've sent it off to a service center
because it needs some repair that you're
not able to do in house, you can
certainly take that pipette and deactivate
it. Once that pipette's returned to you,
you can come back to this configuration
pipettes screen. You can click on the
filter icon and click on show inactive
items. Select your inactive device and
reactivate it. Now, the reason why
deactivation is important is because you
don't want that pipe pet to show up as
being due because it's out at the
service center. When it comes back, of
course, it will be due again. But while
it's at the service center, maybe you
don't want to have it show as due. But
let's say the service center returned
that pipette to you and they said it's too
old to repair. You need to purchase a
new one. In that particular case, you
can deactivate and then subsequently
retire a pipeet. So let me show you how
to do that. Again, in the configuration
screen in the pipettes section, if you
select the pipette that you wish to
retire,
you can click on the deactivate selected
pipette icon and say yes. And you'll
notice that this pipette is showing as
inactive because I selected the filter
to show inactive items.
If you don't see that pipette showing as
inactive, just go ahead and click on
that filter and go ahead and select show
inactive items. Now, once you've
deactivated the pipette, there's one more
step to retiring it. You have to select
the pipette and then click on the retire
selected pipette icon. Now, the moment you
click on that retire pipette, it's very,
very important. The software is going to
ask you, are you sure that retiring is
what you want to do? The moment you
retire anything within the Arttowelware
application, you cannot unretire it. And
that includes the retiring of pipettes. So
the good news is is you can still see
all of your historical calibration data
for that pipette, but that pipette will
never show up as due and it's
essentially being removed from your
inventory list, if you will, as being an
active device. So, the software is just
asking you a very, very important
question, and it's letting you know that
retiring a pipette permanently disables it
in the software. Again, you can still
access those results, though. So, we're
going to go ahead and select okay. And
now you can see the status of the pipead
has changed from inactive to retired.
Okay, that concludes our brief tutorial.
Do you have additional questions? Please

option 3 or at support at aic

Thank you.
